subject: religious-studies
topicName: The Six Articles and Five Roots

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sunni and Shi'a Muslims have different frameworks for their core beliefs. Sunni Islam is based on the Six Articles of Faith ; Shi'a Islam is based on the Five Roots of Usul ad-Din . They share most beliefs but emphasise different aspects.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Both traditions share belief in Tawhid, prophethood and the afterlife. The key difference is the Imamate — Shi'a Muslims believe God appointed twelve Imams as spiritual leaders after Muhammad, while Sunni Muslims do not accept this. Sunni Islam includes belief in angels and holy books as separate articles; Shi'a Islam combines prophethood into one root.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — The Six Articles and Five Roots
steps.body: 1. For The Six Articles and Five Roots questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of The Six Articles and Five Roots to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: When a Sunni Muslim recites the Shahadah, they are affirming the first two Articles of Faith simultaneously: belief in Allah and belief in Muhammad as a prophet. This is why the Shahadah is the foundation of Islamic faith and practice.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
